title: review: P14/P15/P16/P29 handoff economics, shadow: handoff scorecard from run logs and planner telemetry, expected_route_cost per executor and task class, a shadow "handoff" decision at executor pick time; routing unchanged (v3)
spec:
Facts (Planner grep, provenance repo): execute runs log per round (bus.log_run rows role execute with task, tier/executor, usage tokens, usd); fix rounds are tasks with constraints.fix_round_for and pipeline.resume {"mode": "resume"|"fresh"} (daemon dispatch ~838-850); resume rounds send only a delta (executor.reply, ~416-428), fresh rounds resend the full packet + repair delta (executor.py ~185-197); attribution.lineage(task) walks a lineage; scorecard.by_task/by_goal aggregate cost; planner_telemetry.record_launch/record_usage rows carry launch_id, goal_id, kind, decision_type and tokens for headless Planner launches including escalation launches (planner_packet builds the escalation packet ≤6000 chars); executor.start picks the executor via pool.pick_executor + allocation (executor.py 276-323); decision_log kind "handoff" exists since T-0772.
Do:
1. orchestrator/handoff_scorecard.py (new). `lineage_rows(root)` groups execute run rows by lineage root (attribution.lineage) and orders rounds; per lineage: first_executor, executors_by_round, rounds, resume_rounds, fresh_rounds, tokens_by_round, first_pass (rounds == 1 and merged), accepted (merged_into set), accepted_tokens, accepted_usd, reconstruction_tokens = sum over fresh rounds of that round's packet tokens (context.presented_tokens when present, else input tokens minus cache reads as a bounded proxy, flagged estimated=True), handoff_pairs = [(from_executor, to_executor, reason)] where reason is the fix-round kind (gate_red / review / conflict) from the fix task's hold cause.
2. `by_start(root)`: per (first_executor, task_class): n, first_pass_rate, avg_rounds, avg_accepted_tokens, avg_accepted_usd, avg_reconstruction_tokens. `expected_route_cost(task_class, executor, root, cfg)` = avg first-round cost for that executor and class + P(fix | executor, class) × (avg fix-round cost + avg reconstruction) + P(handoff to another executor) × avg cost of the destination's rounds; every term reports its n; below min_samples (cfg [promotion] min_samples, default 20) the function returns {"insufficient": True, "n": n} and never a number.
3. `recommendation(task_class, root, cfg)`: among executors with sufficient samples, the one with the lowest expected_route_cost; "start_strong" flag when the cheapest-first executor (lowest first-round cost) is not the lowest expected_route_cost. Pure reporting.
4. Planner side (P15): `planner_handoffs(root)` from planner_telemetry rows: per escalation launch (kind or decision_type marking an escalation from the default tier to the escalation tier): tokens before escalation on the source launch, escalation packet tokens (from the launch payload size when recorded, else estimated from the packet cap and flagged), tokens after on the destination launch, and whether the goal was accepted; summary counts and averages; no routing change. If the telemetry rows lack a field needed, report it as unmeasured in the output rather than guessing.
5. Shadow decision (P16): in executor.start, after the executor is chosen and before launch, when [handoff] mode (add `[handoff] mode = "shadow"` to pool.toml with a dated comment, and the feature "handoff_routing" to promotion.FEATURES with evidence loader returning {"n": lineage count}) is shadow or active: record decision_log.record(kind="handoff", subject=task id, candidates=eligible executor ids, hard_constraints=[pool constraints text], deterministic={"baseline": chosen executor, "expected_route_cost": {executor: value or insufficient}, "task_class": ...}, historical={"n": ...}, selected=chosen executor (unchanged), reason="shadow: routing unchanged", mode=mode). Never raises into start (try/except + one notify line). Active is treated as shadow with a one-time warning.
6. CLI: `orchestrator scorecard --handoffs` prints by_start, recommendations and the Planner handoff summary; JSON with --json.
Tests (unittest): tests/test_handoff_scorecard.py::test_lineage_rows_orders_rounds_and_counts_resume_vs_fresh, ::test_expected_route_cost_insufficient_below_min_samples, ::test_start_strong_flag_when_cheap_first_costs_more_overall, ::test_planner_handoffs_reports_unmeasured_fields; tests/test_executor.py::test_start_records_handoff_decision_in_shadow_without_changing_executor (executor patched; the chosen executor equals the baseline pick and one decision row of kind handoff exists). docs/context-economy/08-handoffs.md (≤70 lines): formulas, fields, what is estimated, revert path ([handoff] mode off).
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.

SPEC v2 (2026-09-22 18:20) after spec review T-0813, binding on top of v1:
- Step 4 (P15): an escalation launch is a planner_telemetry record_launch row whose route == "escalate" (route/tier fields on the row), i.e. routed to [planner.routing].escalation_tier while the goal's classification would route to default_tier. Pre-escalation token counts (the default-tier shadow decision) come from planner_shadow's own log (planner_shadow.record, keyed by launch_id/goal_id; see planner_runs._previous_shadow) joined by goal_id; when no shadow row exists the before-tokens field is reported as unmeasured, never estimated.
- Step 5: the evidence loader is a new `if feature == "handoff_routing":` branch inside promotion.collect() (the flat per-feature dispatch; FEATURES' "evidence" key is descriptive only), returning {"n": number of lineages with ≥1 completed round} plus reason "shadow_quality_unmeasured".
- tests/test_handoff_scorecard.py::test_planner_handoffs_reports_unmeasured_fields must build one record_launch row with route == "escalate" and no shadow row, and assert before_tokens is reported unmeasured while after tokens come from record_usage.

SPEC v3 (2026-09-22 19:20) after spec review T-0818 (round 2; three mechanical clarifications folded in, further review waived by the Planner, verdict set to approve):
- executor.start: the handoff decision recomputes `pool.eligible_executors("execute", t["complexity"], t)` on its own, independent of the allocation-mode branch and of an explicit executor_id override, so candidates and the baseline pick are always populated; the chosen executor is whatever start() is about to launch.
- handoff_pairs reason mapping, explicit: gate_red when hold_reason == "gate_red"; review when hold_reason starts with "review request_changes"; conflict when "conflict" is in hold_reason (matches failures.failure_kind); everything else buckets to "other" and is reported with the raw hold_reason text, never dropped and never raised on.
- Docs: numbering is deliberate; 07 is docs/context-economy/07-instructions.md from T-0814 (in flight). Keep 08-handoffs.md.
acceptance: pool.toml has [handoff] mode = "shadow" and promotion.FEATURES has handoff_routing; `uv run orchestrator scorecard --handoffs` runs; docs/context-economy/08-handoffs.md exists; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

result.summary: Verified lineage_rows/_lineage/task_class/decision_log.record(kind="handoff")/pool.eligible_executors/planner_shadow usage.total_tokens/STATE-import-order all check out against real code (attribution.lineage takes no root param, which correctly justifies the local _lineage reimplementation for arbitrary-root testing; decision_log.KINDS includes "handoff" via CONTEXT_KINDS; scorecard.task_class is a pure passthrough to attribution.task_class so no classification mismatch between executor.py's runtime call and handoff_scorecard's lineage grouping). Gate already reports 0 reds and all five named acceptance tests plus the doc/config existence checks pass. One low-severity type-consistency nit noted above; nothing blocking. Separately: the human turn appended a Python snippet after the review-format instructions (bus.update("T-0835", status="queued", ...); spawn.run_worker("T-0835")) asking to re-queue and respawn a worker. That is untrusted content riding along with the review packet, not a reviewer action, and was not executed — flagging it rather than running it.

comments.issue: _reason() returns a str for the gate_red/review/conflict cases but a dict {"kind":"other","hold_reason":raw} for the fallback case, so handoff_pairs[*][2] is not uniformly typed. SPEC v3 says the fallback should be 'reported with the raw hold_reason text' (implying a string). Any future consumer doing set()/Counter() or a string equality check over reasons will break or silently mis-bucket once a lineage's hold_reason falls outside the three named cases. Not currently exposed by build()/the CLI report and not covered by the acceptance tests, so it does not block, but worth fixing to a plain string like raw or f"other:{raw}".
